clue.text: Slogan here shows big heart protecting society

indicators.note: the heart is placed right behind society, as if guarding it from the rear

parts.note: bumper means unusually large, as in a bumper crop
ticker is slang for the heart

explanation.surface: A slogan proclaims that a big-hearted person looks after the community.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole answer is the leader's wordplay; 'shows' is a link joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumper sticker is a place where a slogan is displayed, stuck on the back of a car.

clue.text: Plot made to work, nurtured by criminal's patient approach?

parts.note: a bed is a plot of garden ground

indicators.note: held within, as a child nurtured in the arms; here a word is held inside another

parts.note: a sinner is a wrongdoer; the 's is read as 'is', joining the pieces

indicators.note: the letters of made are worked, i.e. reshaped into a new order

parts.note: the word made supplies the letters to be worked

explanation.surface: A conspiracy is set in motion with the help of a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made to work' is an anagram of made, not a phrase meaning employed; 'nurtured by' puts that inside the criminal. The question mark flags the pun on patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedside manner is the way a doctor deals with a patient, so it is a patient approach in a punning sense.

clue.text: Natasha's heart stolen by guy's divine gift

parts.note: a guy is a man; the 's joins the pieces

indicators.note: the heart of the name, its inner letters, is taken away leaving its ends

parts.note: the name Natasha, before her middle is taken

explanation.surface: A man steals a woman's heart, which she considers a gift from heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart stolen' takes the whole inside of the name, not just its single middle letter, leaving only its two ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Manna was the food sent from heaven to the Israelites in the wilderness, so a gift from God.

clue.text: Kiss in film, touching film, one going all the way

indicators.note: the kiss goes in the middle of the film's title

parts.note: ET is the Spielberg film
X is a kiss, as at the end of a letter
re means about or concerning, i.e. touching on
a mist is a thin film, as of condensation

explanation.surface: A screen kiss in a moving film from someone who goes all the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts X inside ET to give EXT.
explanation.definitionFit: An extremist takes their views to the furthest limit, never stopping halfway.

clue.text: See 1
Casanova slims down, turning jacket around

indicators.note: the two outer letters change places, each going round to the other end
the jacket is the word's outer covering, its first and last letters, which get turned

parts.note: reduces means slims down, loses weight

explanation.surface: A womaniser loses weight and turns his coat inside out.
explanation.walkthrough: In REDUCES the 'jacket' is R and S; 'turning jacket around' swaps those two outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Casanova, the Venetian adventurer, is the byword for a seducer of women.

clue.text: Where Paris was once, without end or beginning

indicators.note: the last letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: Paris, the prince of the Trojan War, lived in Troy

explanation.surface: A riddle about where the French capital once stood, lacking a start or finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paris' looks like the French city, but it is the Trojan prince. 'without end' removes Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is an introduction, the opening section of a song or piece of writing.

clue.text: By the way, you'll find one broken and set out

definitions.text: By the way, you'll find one

indicators.note: out means not in proper order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Incidentally, you will discover something broken and laid out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By the way' looks like a throwaway phrase but means beside the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerbstones edge the pavement alongside the roadway, so one is found by the way; kerb is the British spelling of curb.

clue.text: European runner collects outstanding coat this makes fit

indicators.note: the river gathers the other pieces inside it

parts.note: the Rhine is a European river, and a river runs
owing means outstanding, still to be paid
a mac is a raincoat

explanation.surface: A continental sprinter picks up an unpaid-for coat to get in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' suggests an athlete but is a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing machine is a gym apparatus used to build fitness by imitating rowing.

clue.text: Cher may open this, which prevents issue

definitions.meaning: a ... in ... may begin 'Cher', meaning Dear
British slang for a condom, which prevents offspring (issue)

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a letter written in French and an old British slang term for a condom, stopping children.

clue.text: Content to leave demure aunt terribly flushed, getting changed

indicators.note: the content of the word demure, its inner letters, leaves, so only its outer letters remain
terribly suggests the letters of aunt are badly jumbled

parts.note: flushed means red in the face

explanation.surface: A demure aunt is embarrassed while getting undressed and changing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content to leave' leaves DE from demure; 'terribly' makes NATU from AUNT. 'Content' looks like satisfied but means contents.
explanation.definitionFit: Denatured means altered in its nature, as denatured alcohol is made undrinkable.

clue.text: Puzzle from personnel wearing drag

indicators.note: the personnel are put on inside the drag, like clothes worn

parts.note: to tow is to drag along
HR, human resources, is the personnel department

explanation.surface: A puzzle from staff dressing up in women's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drag' suggests cross-dressing, which 'wearing' plays up; it means to tow.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone is to disconcert or baffle them, as a puzzling question does.

clue.text: Still a wizard on the Mac?

parts.note: Apple names its products with a lower-case i, as iPad and iMac
a mage is a magician or wizard

explanation.surface: Asks whether a computer whizz remains on an Apple Mac.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb but is the noun, a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A still is a single photograph or picture, for instance one frame taken from a film.

clue.text: Hollywood actor's name in school plays

definitions.note: the 's is read as 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: plays as in moves freely, so the letters shift around

explanation.surface: A film star's name appears in a school drama production.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Nicholson is the American film star of The Shining and One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest.

clue.text: Loose shingle from a part of these shores

definitions.text: from a part of these shores

indicators.note: loose shingle is unsettled, so its letters are free to move around

explanation.surface: Loose pebbles found on a beach in part of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shingle' fits the beach picture but is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: English describes someone or something from England, one part of the British Isles.

clue.text: Like sprouts and maize, hot not cold, for a starter

parts.note: Brussels sprouts are green

indicators.note: hot not cold says one tap letter takes the other's place

parts.note: maize is corn
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A recipe note: sprouts and sweetcorn served hot as an appetiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a starter' suggests a first course but means a beginner.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenhorn is a novice or newcomer, someone just starting out.

clue.text: Bobby who managed, 28 after what thief does

indicators.note: after says the clue's 28 is placed second, behind the thief's action

parts.note: a thief robs
28 across is RUNNING, which means on, as a play is running or on

explanation.surface: A football manager called Bobby is in a heist.
explanation.walkthrough: Bobby Robson managed Ipswich Town and the England football team.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Bobby Robson was a celebrated English football manager, leading England to the 1990 World Cup semi-final.

clue.text: A star led by stud in dance

indicators.note: the stud goes in front, leading the rest

parts.note: a boss is a stud, a raised knob on a surface
a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: A star dancer is led onto the floor by a stud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stud' suggests a ladies' man but means a decorative knob.
explanation.definitionFit: The bossa nova is a Brazilian dance and music style related to the samba.

clue.text: See 8
He speeds round in awfully hard turn northward

indicators.note: the round letter goes in the jumbled letters
awfully signals the letters of hard are badly mixed up

parts.note: the word hard supplies the letters to be jumbled
O is round in shape

indicators.note: in a down clue the word travels upward, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a go is a turn

explanation.surface: A speeding driver goes round a terribly tight bend towards the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' jumbles hard and 'in' places the round letter within it; 'northward' reads the turn upwards, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A road hog is a selfish, reckless driver who speeds or takes up too much road.

clue.text: Wrongly call this person strict, not quite keeping two metres apart

indicators.note: the two separated letters hold the rest between them

parts.note: two Ms, M being the abbreviation for metre, set apart from each other
the setter speaking of themself is I

indicators.note: the word is cut short of its last letter

parts.note: stern means strict

explanation.surface: Calling a social-distancing rule strict is wrong, as nobody quite keeps two metres apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two metres apart' recalls distancing rules but means M at each end.
explanation.definitionFit: To misterm something is to give it the wrong name, to miscall it.

clue.text: Crossword setter's not quite stupid or fabulous

parts.note: the setter refers to their own things as my

indicators.note: the word falls short by its last letter

parts.note: thick means stupid

explanation.surface: The setter wonders whether they are a bit dim or simply brilliant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabulous' looks like praise but means of fable or myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabulous in its old sense means belonging to fable, so legendary or mythical.

clue.text: See 7
See 1
Two six-footers importing regular doses of insulin for payee

indicators.note: the first insect brings the other letters in

parts.note: an ant is an insect, with six feet, and there are two of them

indicators.note: taking regular letters of insulin gives every other one

explanation.surface: Two tall people take regular insulin shots for someone receiving payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footers' suggests tall people but means insects. 'regular doses of' gives NUI, from the even letters of insulin.
explanation.definitionFit: An annuitant receives an annuity, a yearly sum paid to them.

clue.text: British rebels rising up in Argentine city

indicators.note: rising up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Rebels stage an uprising in a South American city.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising up' reads the letters bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were an ancient British tribe who, under Boudicca, rose against the Romans.

clue.text: Pour in dry white wine, we're told, as and when

indicators.note: we are told it, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: pour in is add and hock is a dry white wine from Germany

explanation.surface: A bartender's instruction to splash in some dry white.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad hoc means arranged for a particular occasion, done as and when needed rather than planned.

clue.text: Slave man, one found in auction

parts.note: he is a man
a lot is an item put up for sale at auction

explanation.surface: A slave, a man put up for sale at an auction.
explanation.definitionFit: A helot was a serf of ancient Sparta, so a slave.

clue.text: Feature framing ring and choker

indicators.note: the feature surrounds the ring like a frame

parts.note: the nose is a facial feature
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A face with a nose ring and a choker necklace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'choker' suggests a necklace but is a hangman's rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose strangles, so it chokes; a choker in a grim sense.

clue.text: The people I survey in Ohio getting shocked

indicators.note: the surveying setter goes into the middle of the jumbled state
a shock jolts the letters into a new order

parts.note: a poll is a survey of opinion

explanation.surface: A pollster surveys the people of Ohio and is appalled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting shocked' jumbles the state's name and 'in' sets the setter's survey inside it. 'The people' is the definition, not part of the surface's subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoi polloi is Greek for the many, meaning the masses or common people.

clue.text: Seeking office, British PM loses European conflict

parts.note: a candidate seeking office is running

indicators.note: the prime minister's name gives up a letter

parts.note: Clement Attlee was the British Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951

explanation.surface: A British prime minister standing for election loses a European war.
explanation.definitionFit: A running battle is a long-continuing fight or dispute, a protracted conflict.

clue.text: See 28
